# Overview of Part 04: Statistics & Probability

This guide synthesizes the mathematical and programmatic foundations from Part 04:

1. **`01_descriptive_stats_and_distributions.R`** — Robust estimators, correlation, the `d/p/q/r` probability distribution system, and Monte Carlo simulations.
2. **`02_hypothesis_testing_and_anova.R`** — Parametric and non-parametric hypothesis testing (`t.test`, `wilcox.test`, `prop.test`, `aov`, `TukeyHSD`, and `p.adjust`).
3. **`03_regression_and_glm.R`** — Ordinary Least Squares (`lm`), Generalized Linear Models (`glm`), model diagnostics, and Bootstrap resampling.

---

# Probability Distributions & The Central Limit Theorem

Every distribution in R follows the four-prefix convention:

- `d<dist>(x)`: Probability Density / Mass Function $f(x)$
- `p<dist>(q)`: Cumulative Distribution Function $F(q) = P(X \le q)$
- `q<dist>(p)`: Quantile Function $F^{-1}(p)$
- `r<dist>(n)`: Random Variate Generator

```{r clt-simulation}
set.seed(42)
pop_draws  <- rexp(10000, rate = 0.5)
clt_means  <- replicate(4000, mean(rexp(40, rate = 0.5)))

old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 3, 1.2))
hist(pop_draws, breaks = 40, freq = FALSE, col = "#fc8d62", border = "white",
     main = "Skewed Population: Exp(rate = 0.5)", xlab = "Value")
hist(clt_means, breaks = 35, freq = FALSE, col = "#66c2a5", border = "white",
     main = "Sample Means (n = 40) -> Normal!", xlab = "Sample Mean")
curve(dnorm(x, mean = 2, sd = 2 / sqrt(40)), add = TRUE, col = "navy", lwd = 2.5)
par(old_par)
```

# Hypothesis Testing Decision Matrix

| Goal | Parametric Test | Non-Parametric Counterpart |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Compare 2 Independent Means/Locations** | `t.test(y ~ group)` (Welch) | `wilcox.test(y ~ group)` (Mann-Whitney U) |
| **Compare Paired Measurements** | `t.test(y1, y2, paired = TRUE)` | `wilcox.test(y1, y2, paired = TRUE)` |
| **Compare $\ge 3$ Independent Groups** | `aov(y ~ group)` + `TukeyHSD()` | `kruskal.test(y ~ group)` |
| **Categorical Association / Proportions** | `chisq.test()`, `prop.test()` | `fisher.test()` (exact for small counts) |

# Linear & Generalized Linear Regression Diagnostics

```{r regression-diagnostics, fig.height=7}
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt * hp, data = mtcars)
knitr::kable(round(coef(summary(fit)), 4), caption = "OLS Regression Coefficients (`mpg ~ wt * hp`)")

# Standard 4-Panel Diagnostic Plot
old_par <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 2.5, 1.2))
plot(fit, pch = 19, col = "#2b8cbe")
par(old_par)
```
